content: How's this one going? It's starting to look pretty good to me. Anything pending, @Chris Henson @Haoxuan Yin?

I've just not had a chance to re-review since the last changes, though taking a glance now I think my biggest comments were addressed. If you have time to have a look yourself, I'd appreciate it, as my time is a little more constrained now.
Thanks, good to know the biggest comments are addressed. I'll have a look as soon as I can.

@Haoxuan Yin I'm done reading. A minor comment is that we should try to golf/automate more some proofs, but it's good enough for now I think.

It'd be good to have a proof that the new AlphaEquiv is equal to the old AlphaEquiv (which could be called 'TraditionalAlphaEquiv' or whatever), proving that the new method matches what lambda calculus people expect. It looks kinda obvious given all the results you have. Or am I missing some challenge?
